g.title: cluster_enum
g.text: Otherwise: list the candidates, newest version first

g.title: cluster_checks
g.text: (each check can reject it; then the next-newest candidate is tried)

g.title: vocab
g.text: the package being planned whose dependency list we are reading
one line of that list asks for
one concrete version of the child, taken from the tree
all atoms for that child from the parent's list, merged

g.title: slot
g.text: Step 3 begins: the parent needs the child
; which slot of the child does the request mean?
merge the slot parts of all atoms (":6", ":=", ":0/2=", ":*"); if the request says ":="
and a version of the child was already chosen for this parent, lock onto that sub-slot

g.title: reuse
g.text: Was a version of the child already chosen for another parent in this proof,
and does it fit this parent's request too?
answered from the proof's constraint store (keyed by
) — one lookup, no scan of the proof

g.title: reused
g.text: its version was already verified when first chosen, so the version checks below are skipped

g.title: t0
g.text: not masked, not a binary package, right slot;
when the child is the parent's own package (self-dependency),
the parent's version only counts if it is already installed (bootstrap)

g.title: c6
g.text: Does the candidate accept the parent in return?
if the candidate's own RDEPEND names the parent's package, the parent's version must satisfy it

g.title: t1
g.text: : any keyword accepted, still not masked

g.title: t0->t1
g.text: only when the whole proof (or step 7) runs in that tier

g.title: t1->t2
g.text: only when the whole proof (or step 7) runs in that tier

g.title: virt
g.text: For virtual/* only: try providers we are already installing first

g.title: c1
g.text: Is this candidate the parent's own version?
(self-dependency) then only if it is already installed

g.title: c2
g.text: Does its version satisfy every bound of the request?

g.title: c3
g.text: Is it inside the allowed range for this package?
= this request ∩ what the proof context already demands ∩ what failed passes taught us

g.title: c4
g.text: Was it ruled out by an earlier failed pass, or by a build-failure fixup?

g.title: c5
g.text: Is there an equally valid other version of the child whose own version pins agree with what we chose?
then step aside for it (e.g. opam-installer-2.5 yields to 2.3 when opam-common is locked at 2.3)

g.title: c7
g.text: Can it be built with the USE flags this request demands?
bracket flags ("[ssl,-static]") must be settable; REQUIRED_USE must still hold; "[flag=]" ties
are followed; a shared provider that must gain a flag is scheduled for a forced rebuild

g.title: tag
g.text: : accept this keyword, unmask this, accept this license, change these USE flags

g.title: act
g.text: Is a copy installed in the same slot?

g.title: out
g.text: Hand the result to the prover
"this package is now fixed to this version" + the range this edge demands + the USE flags to build with + the action.
The prover merges these into the shared constraint store; if they clash with another edge's choice,
it learns the range and restarts the pass (the same retry as steps 4-6)

g.title: elig
g.text: Later, when the chosen entry's own rule runs, visibility is checked once more
masked or unkeyworded entries pass only under the relaxation tier, the step-7 override,
or when this is a same-version ABI repair of an installed package
